To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a multiplex PCR for the demonstration of t(11; 14) and t(14; 18) in PB and BM samples allows for a rapid and sensitive detection of BCL1/IGH and IGH/BCL-2 gene rearrangements.
we developed a fast and high throughput multiplex PCR for the demonstration of BCL-2 and BCL-1 rearrangements in NHL, and that this approach has clinical relevance.
we have designed a multiple PCR, which is able to identify BCL-1 and BCL-1 gene fusions in mantle cell and follicular non Hodgkin’s lymphoma, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of B- and T-cell non-Hodgkins lymphomas (NHL), and with the application of this research in the diagnosis and treatment of NHL patients.
the development of a multiplex PCR for detection of BCL2 and BCL1 translocations, and the validation of the PCR assay by comparing the PCR results to conventional diagnostic methods.
the molecular characterization of BCL-2 and BCL-1 gene rearrangements in non-Hodgkins lymphoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this multiplex PCR approach is a very useful and sensitive tool in the diagnosis of B-cell NHL, especially in cases where the diagnosis is uncertain or the disease is atypical.
the multiplex PCR assay is a valuable addition to the diagnostic work up of NHL.
the Bcl-1/IGH PCR is a useful diagnostic tool for the detection of t(11; 14)-positive mantle cell lymphoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multiplex PCR is a fast and highly sensitive method for the detection of the BCL1/IGH and/or BCL2/IGH translocation in patients with NHL.

this PCR is a very sensitive and specific method for the detection of t(11; 14) in mantle cell lymphomas and for t(14; 18) in follicular lymphomas, which is important in the differential diagnosis of these lymphomas and in the evaluation of the prognosis.
the PCR approach is a useful tool for the detection of molecular lesions in blood and bone marrow, which have diagnostic importance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular diagnosis of mantle cell- and/or follicular lymphoma is possible with high sensitivity and specificity in blood and/or bone marrow.
this multiplex PCR assay can identify patients with a high probability of NHL, even when the diagnosis is uncertain by morphology, immunophenotype or molecular analysis.
the molecular detection of t(11; 14) and t(14; 18) in PB and/or bone marrow is a sensitive and specific diagnostic tool in patients with NHL.
